diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Lambda function can be created before its AMI-housekeeper inline policy is attached. Make the function depend on this policy so its execution role permissions are established before the function is ready to be invoked.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Lambda function should wait for its AMI-housekeeper inline policy to be attached before it can be invoked with the permissions this function needs; referencing only the execution role does not order this policy creation. Add an explicit dependency because there is no suitable Lambda argument to reference this policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Lambda function's AMI cleanup behavior requires the inline cleanup policy to be installed before the function can run successfully, but the graph does not order function creation after that policy.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When tracing is enabled, the Lambda function can be created before its X-Ray inline policy is attached, leaving tracing enabled without the required execution permissions. Order the function after this policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When tracing is enabled, the Lambda function needs the X-Ray role policy before it handles traced invocations. Its role reference does not imply ordering on this separate inline policy resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
When X-Ray tracing is enabled, the function's X-Ray policy should be installed before the function is used with tracing; no dependency on this policy is expressed.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When VPC subnets are configured, Lambda creation can race ahead of attachment of AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole. Lambda needs these EC2 permissions to configure its VPC networking, so it should depend on this attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
For VPC-configured Lambda functions, the execution role needs the VPC access policy before Lambda configures networking. The role-name reference does not order this separate policy attachment before function creation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Lambda function uses VPC configuration when subnet and security-group IDs are supplied, but it does not wait for the VPC execution policy attachment. Ensure the execution role has the required ENI permissions before creating the VPC-enabled function.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper` has a `vpc_config` block (subnets/security groups as soon as subnets are configured) but no dependency on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role`, which grants the execution role `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole`. Both only depend on the shared `aws_iam_role.ami_housekeeper`, so Terraform may create the function before the policy attachment exists and CreateFunction fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2". The function should be ordered after the attachment (the AWS provider docs include `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.lambda_logs` in the function's `depends_on`). No clean attribute reference exists on the function to express this, so a bare `depends_on` is appropriate.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper defines a vpc_config (subnet_ids/security_group_ids) but has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role. When Lambda creates a function in a VPC it assumes the execution role to create network interfaces; if the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy is not yet attached to aws_iam_role.ami_housekeeper, function creation fails with 'The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2'. Both resources only reference var.lambda_subnet_ids, so nothing orders the policy attachment before the function. Add an explicit dependency (or otherwise ensure the attachment is applied first).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper is configured with a vpc_config (active whenever var.lambda_subnet_ids is non-empty), which requires the execution role to already have the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy so Lambda can create ENIs. The function only depends on aws_iam_role.ami_housekeeper (the bare role), not on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role. If Terraform creates the function before that attachment, function creation fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface". Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role].

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EventBridge target can be installed before the Lambda resource-based permission, allowing an enabled rule to attempt invocation before it is authorized. Order target creation after the permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EventBridge target can be installed before the Lambda invoke permission, even though that permission is required for the rule to invoke the function. Order target creation after the permission to avoid a window where scheduled invocations are unauthorized.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target can be installed before the Lambda resource-based permission, leaving scheduled invocations unauthorized until that permission is created. Order target creation after the permission.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper is created before its CloudWatch Logs permissions: the implicit ordering chain is lambda -> aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper -> aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging (the policy embeds the log group ARN, and the log group's name references the function). At function creation time the execution role therefore cannot yet write logs; a first invocation could fail to create log streams. A bare depends_on on aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging would normally close this, but note that in the current configuration it would create a cycle (log group -> function) until the log group's name is decoupled from the function (see the related finding on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper depends only on the execution role, not on aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging, which grants the role the CloudWatch Logs permissions (logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents, scoped to the log group ARN) the function needs when it first runs. Terraform applies the function and the inline policy in parallel (both only depend on the role), so an early invocation can fail with access-denied on logging. The function should also depend on the logging policy; there is no attribute on the function that can reference the policy, so a bare depends_on is required.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper currently depends on aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper (its name references aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper.function_name), so the function is created first and the managed log group afterwards. If the function is invoked in that window (it is wired to a scheduled EventBridge rule), Lambda auto-creates /aws/lambda/<name> with default settings, which then collides with this resource ("The specified log group already exists"). The documented pattern is to pre-create the log group and add a bare depends_on on the function. Note: adding that depends_on requires first decoupling the log group's name from the function — e.g. name = "/aws/lambda/${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper", which matches function_name = "${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper" — otherwise a cycle would result.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper does not depend on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper, but the log group must exist before the function is invoked: if Lambda is invoked while the Terraform-managed log group is absent, the Lambda service auto-creates a default /aws/lambda/<function_name> log group (no retention policy, default encryption, STANDARD class), and the subsequent create of aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper then fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException — so the intended retention_in_days, kms_key_id, and log_group_class settings are never applied. The current graph only has the reverse edge (the log group's name references aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper.function_name), which forces the function to be created first. A bare depends_on on the function would create a cycle with that name reference; the recommended fix is to compute the function name in a local (e.g. local.function_name = "${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper"), use it for both the function_name and the log group name, and add depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper] to the lambda function.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper is created before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.ami_housekeeper (the log group references the function's name, inverting the required order). Lambda auto-creates a default log group (no retention, no KMS) on first log write, so an invocation arriving before the log group is provisioned either yields a log group with the wrong settings or makes the log group's own create fail with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The function must be ordered after the log group; since the log group currently references the function's name (which would create a cycle), the name should be computed directly (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.prefix}-ami-housekeeper") and the function given a bare depends_on on the log group.
